name: CommonsenseQA
description: A challenging dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions that require commonsense knowledge to answer. Questions are generated from ConceptNet by extracting subgraphs with one source concept and three target concepts sharing the same semantic relation, encouraging workers to create questions with complex semantics requiring prior knowledge.

creator.name: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
creator.affiliation: Tel-Aviv University and Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence

citeAs: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant. 2019. CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv:1811.00937v2 [cs.CL]
rai:dataCollection: Data collection involved extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet knowledge base, where each subgraph contains one source concept (question concept) and three target concepts (answer concepts) connected by the same semantic relation. Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were then asked to author multiple-choice questions based on these concept sets.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base containing 32 million triplets representing natural language concepts and commonsense relations. The dataset filtered ConceptNet to 236,208 triplets using specific criteria, resulting in approximately 130,000 triplets (43,000 question sets) for potential question generation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered using the following steps: (1) Filtered triplets with general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or relations already well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA), using 22 relations in total; (2) Filtered triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English; (3) Filtered triplets where the edit distance between c1 and c2 is too low. This resulted in 236,208 triplets from the original 32 million.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question sets were created by grouping three different triplets with the same question concept and relation but different answer concepts. This generates three answer concepts that are semantically similar and have a similar relation to the question concept. The procedure generated approximately 130,000 triplets (43,000 question sets) for potential question generation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers saw the question concept and three answer concepts for each question set. They were asked to formulate three questions, where all questions contain the question concept and each question should have as an answer one of the answer concepts, but not the other two. Workers were instructed to avoid using words that have a strong relation to the answer concept. For each formulated question, workers added two additional distractors: one selected from ConceptNet answer concepts with the same relation, and one formulated manually. Each question is accompanied with five candidate answers total (one correct answer and four distractors).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers from a disjoint group of verifiers. Verifiers annotate a question as unanswerable or choose the right answer. Only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly were used. This verification process filtered out 15% of the questions. A total of 12,247 final examples were generated from 16,242 that were formulated.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was verified by 2 workers. For human evaluation, 100 random questions were sampled and each question gathered answers from five workers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Only AMT annotators for which at least 75% of the questions they formulate pass the verification process were accepted. 122 formulators contributed to question generation, with 10 workers formulating more than 85% of the questions. For human evaluation testing, workers were not involved in question generation, were not AMT master workers, and did not use a qualification test.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance natural language understanding systems' ability to reason with commonsense knowledge, which is a critical component for understanding human language and behavior. Questions often require background knowledge about spatial relations, causes and effects, scientific facts and social conventions that are trivial for humans but challenging for current NLU systems.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset builds on ConceptNet, which may contain biases inherent in its knowledge representation. The top-5 question concepts are 'Person' (3.1%), 'People' (2.0%), 'Human' (0.7%), 'Water' (0.5%) and 'Cat' (0.5%), showing some concentration in certain concept types. 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, which may introduce individual annotator biases.
rai:dataLimitations: Analysis of 100 development set examples revealed several limitations: (1) Models perform well (77.7% accuracy) on examples with surface clues; (2) Lower accuracy (42.8%) on examples involving negation or antonyms; (3) Lower accuracy (38.4%) on examples requiring factoid knowledge; (4) Particularly low accuracy (35.4%) on questions where the correct answer has finer granularity compared to distractors; (5) Low accuracy (23.8%) on cases where the correct answer needs to meet a conjunction of conditions. The best model (BERT-LARGE) achieves only 55.9% accuracy compared to 88.9% human accuracy. Learning curves suggest that even with 100k examples, BERT-LARGE accuracy would be roughly 75%, still substantially lower than human performance.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, testing, and validation of commonsense question answering systems. The data is split into training/development/test sets with an 80/10/10 split. Two types of splits are provided: (a) random split where questions are split uniformly at random, and (b) question concept split where each set has disjoint question concepts. The random split is considered the primary split as it is harder for models. The dataset aims to test commonsense knowledge and facilitate future work in incorporating commonsense knowledge into NLU systems.
